analysis.title: Gold Market Commentary | Where floor art thou
key_insights: Gold finished October 2026 at US$3,913/oz, down 6.3% m/m, with declines in all major currencies tracked (EUR -4.7%, JPY -6.2%, GBP -7.2%, CAD -8.0%, CHF -7.5%, INR -5.3%, RMB -5.9%, TRY -4.5%, AUD -7.4%).

The WGC's Gold Return Attribution Model (GRAM) shows lower yields supported gold in October, but gold and yields moved in the same direction, a pattern GRAM does not capture. Likely drivers were Fed rate-path repricing, speculative de-grossing, and a temporary rotation from equities and gold into bonds as stocks fell and credit spreads widened.

Much of the October selling may have been derivatives-led. COMEX managed money net positions fell US$7bn (53t) in October after a larger drop in September. Open interest fell more, as non-reportable and spreading net positions dropped in the last week of October, which contributed to the model's negative residual.
Global gold ETFs recorded US$2bn (16t) of inflows in October despite the price decline. Europe led, then Asia, while North America had a small outflow.

Spot gold is about 25% below its January 2026 all-time high (US$5,405/oz on 29-Jan-26). The WGC argues the post-2011 downturn is a poor parallel and that conditions for recovery are much stronger now.

The WGC framework tests three signals in bear regimes (50-day average below 200-day) since 2005: dislocation (gold well below its 200-day average), dollar strength (DXY rally in the top tier of the past 52 weeks), and positioning washout (speculative futures positions low relative to open interest). A signal fires when in the most extreme 30% of bear-regime months.

Historical results: all bear months had a median 3-month forward return of 3.2% with 63% positive (N=24). With at least 2 of 3 signals: median 4.2%, 90% positive (N=10). With all 3: median 9.8%, 100% positive (N=5). The WGC notes the sample is small.

Two of three conditions are currently met: gold is well below its 200-day average and the dollar has rallied into its top tier. Positioning remains elevated, and a further futures positioning shake-out is needed before a more durable recovery.
The framework covers only the next three months and says nothing about the year ahead. The WGC says it is not a trading rule and does not encourage tactical trading.

The 2011 comparison is described as misplaced. Today real yields are higher (10-year TIPS 2.6% vs 0.1%), HY spreads are tighter (3.3% vs 7.6%), the dollar is expensive (REER 106 vs 82.3), the stock-bond correlation is 0.2 vs -0.6, 10-year inflation expectations are 2.7% vs 1.6%, geopolitical risk is higher (GPR 156 vs 68), and central bank buying is ~800t/yr vs ~500t.

Technically gold is about 10% below its 200-day average, a downside extreme, and sits above the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement of the rise from 2015 at US$3,857/oz. Momentum is still lower, so a test of US$3,857 may yet occur, and the WGC says that level would likely be an attractive entry point for investors.

Event risks in Q4 include US midterm election policy outcomes and geopolitical triggers. Further cracks in equities and credit could make Treasuries more attractive and bring back the positive gold-yield correlation, which depends on the inflation threat fading.
For strategic investors, the WGC says averaging into weakness has historically made sense for an asset that has returned close to 9% a year since 1971.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Month-end price, down 6.3% m/m and 10.4% y-t-d, about 25% below the January 2026 record of US$5,405.
Real yields are in restrictive territory with more room to fall, which the WGC sees as supportive for gold over the medium term.
Spreads are tight, though credit spreads widened during October as stocks fell.
The dollar is expensive, leaving less room to rally than in 2011.
Bonds are a less reliable equity hedge than in 2011 (-0.6).

macro_indicators.indicator: US budget balance to GDP / unemployment rate
macro_indicators.interpretation: Unemployment is low but the deficit remains large.

risk_factors: Momentum remains lower and a test of US$3,857/oz may still occur.
Futures positioning remains elevated, so further liquidation could pressure gold before a durable bottom.
Q4 event risk from US midterm election policy outcomes and geopolitical triggers.
Further equity and credit stress could make Treasuries more attractive and keep gold and yields moving together, which depends on whether the inflation threat fades.
The historical framework rests on only five episodes with all three signals and covers only a three-month horizon.
charts_described: Chart 1 attributes October's gold decline to a rotation into bonds and outflows from North American ETFs and COMEX futures positions, using GRAM driver categories: economic expansion, risk and uncertainty, opportunity cost (FX and rates), momentum and residual.
Figure 2 shows the gold price with a 10% envelope below its 40-week (200-day) average, with data to 28 October 2026.
vol_and_positioning: COMEX managed money net positions fell US$7bn (53t) in October after a larger September drop, but open interest fell more as non-reportable and spreading net positions dropped in the last week of October.
Speculative froth is not fully cleared: positioning remains elevated and a further futures shake-out is needed before a durable recovery.
The WGC's positioning washout signal is defined as speculative positions (managed money plus smaller traders) falling to unusually low levels relative to open interest. It has not yet fired.
Global gold ETFs took in US$2bn (16t) in October. North America had a small outflow.
geopolitical: Geopolitical risk (GPR index 156) is far above the 2011 reading of 68.
Geopolitical triggers and the policy outcomes of the US midterm elections are cited as Q4 event risks that could push gold either way.

tension_points.bull_case: Two of three recovery signals are in place (price well below the 200-day average, dollar in its top tier). Historically 2-of-3 gave a 90% positive hit rate and a 4.2% median 3-month return. Real yields are high with room to fall, central bank buying is ~800t/yr, geopolitical risk is elevated, and ETFs took in US$2bn in October.
tension_points.bear_case: Positioning washout has not occurred and speculative froth remains. Momentum is still lower and a test of US$3,857/oz may come. Q4 event risks and equity and credit stress could push investors into Treasuries and keep gold and yields moving together.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A clear-out in futures positioning while the dollar and dislocation signals hold would complete the setup. A break below the US$3,857/oz Fibonacci support would undercut the interim-bottom case.
